nodes.description: Constant 86400 seconds per day used for time bucketing of the release schedule.
Immutable ERC20 token held in timelock and transferred out on withdrawals.
Immutable beneficiary address receiving released tokens.
Immutable start timestamp (day-aligned) of the release period.
End timestamp of the release period, mutable via terminate().
Total benefit amount; reduced by terminate() to the already released amount.
Running total of tokens already withdrawn by the beneficiary.
Flag marking that the contract has been terminated by the owner.
Beneficiary-facing function that transfers the vested-but-unwithdrawn amount via safeTransfer.
onlyOwner function that truncates the release schedule and sweeps unreleased tokens to the owner.
View computing vested tokens from block.timestamp, release window and total benefit.
View returning _totalBenefit minus releasedBalance().
View returning the accumulated withdrawn balance.
View returning the held ERC20 token reference.
View returning the beneficiary address.
View returning the total benefit amount.
Deploys the timelock, aligns the start time to a day boundary and validates the end time against block.timestamp.
Miner/validator influenced time source used for vesting math and termination.
Caller identity used by the inherited onlyOwner access control through _msgSender().
External ERC20 token transfer performed in withdraw() and terminate(), transferring control to the token contract.
Arithmetic state update _withdrawedBalance += amount in withdraw().
Timestamp-derived day arithmetic ((block.timestamp - _releaseStartTime) / SECONDS_OF_A_DAY and proportional _totalBenefit * passedDays / totalDays) in releasedBalance().
Timestamp truncation arithmetic block.timestamp - (block.timestamp % SECONDS_OF_A_DAY) in terminate().
Balance sweeper arithmetic token().balanceOf(address(this)) - (_totalBenefit - _withdrawedBalance) in terminate().
Constructor parameter for the ERC20 token address assigned to _token.
Constructor parameter for the beneficiary address assigned to _beneficiary.
Constructor parameter for the raw release start time, day-aligned before storage.
Constructor parameter for the timelock length in days used to derive _releaseEndTime.
Constructor parameter for the total benefit assigned to _totalBenefit.
Local amount (releasedBalance() - _withdrawedBalance) transferred in withdraw().
Local surplus amount swept to the owner in terminate().
Local number of elapsed days since _releaseStartTime in releasedBalance().
Local total number of days of the release window in releasedBalance().

edges.reason: constructor assigns parameter token_ to the immutable _token state variable
constructor assigns parameter beneficiary_ to _beneficiary
constructor stores the day-aligned releaseStartTime_ into _releaseStartTime
constructor computes and stores _releaseEndTime from start time and daysOfTimelock_
constructor sets _totalBenefit = totalBenefit_
constructor initializes _withdrawedBalance to zero
constructor initializes _isTerminated to false
constructor require() compares _releaseEndTime against block.timestamp, making deployment time-dependent
constructor parameter token_ flows into the constructor body
constructor parameter beneficiary_ flows into the constructor body
constructor parameter releaseStartTime_ flows into the constructor body
constructor parameter daysOfTimelock_ flows into the constructor body
constructor parameter totalBenefit_ flows into the constructor body
releasedBalance() branches on block.timestamp to decide zero, full or proportional vesting
releasedBalance() reads _releaseStartTime for elapsed-time math
releasedBalance() reads _releaseEndTime to bound the vesting window
releasedBalance() reads _totalBenefit to scale the vested amount
timestamp-derived day calculations in releasedBalance() are collected as an unsafe timestamp operation
local passedDays is computed and used inside releasedBalance()
local totalDays is computed and used inside releasedBalance()
unreleasedBalance() calls releasedBalance()
unreleasedBalance() subtracts releasedBalance() from _totalBenefit
withdraw() invokes releasedBalance() twice for its requirement and amount computation
terminate() invokes releasedBalance() to truncate the remaining benefit
withdraw() reads _withdrawedBalance to compute the withdrawable amount
withdraw() performs the arithmetic state mutation _withdrawedBalance += amount
the unsafe arithmetic update writes into the _withdrawedBalance state variable
local amount is derived from releasedBalance() - _withdrawedBalance inside withdraw()
withdraw() makes an external token transfer (safeTransfer) at the end of its body
the external safeTransfer operates on the _token ERC20 reference
the external safeTransfer in withdraw() sends tokens to _beneficiary
a malicious token can re-enter withdraw() during the external transfer callback
withdraw() calls token() to query balance and perform the transfer
terminate() calls token() to query balance and sweep tokens
terminate() sets _isTerminated = true
terminate() rewrites _totalBenefit to releasedBalance()
terminate() rewrites _releaseEndTime to the current day boundary
terminate() depends on block.timestamp to recompute the end of the release period
terminal timestamp truncation arithmetic is collected as an unsafe timestamp operation
terminate() computes the owner sweep amount from a balance subtraction that can underflow if the token balance is short
terminate() performs an external token transfer to the owner
a malicious token can re-enter terminate() during the external transfer callback
local amountToWithdraw is computed inside terminate() and passed to safeTransfer
terminate() is guarded by the onlyOwner modifier which compares _msgSender() with owner()
token() returns the _token state variable
beneficiary() returns the _beneficiary state variable
totalBenefit() returns the _totalBenefit state variable
withdrawedBalance() returns the _withdrawedBalance state variable
releasedBalance() uses SECONDS_OF_A_DAY to convert elapsed seconds into days
constructor uses SECONDS_OF_A_DAY to align the start time and compute the end time
terminate() uses SECONDS_OF_A_DAY to round the current timestamp down to a day boundary
